newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Hearing delayed for Swiss men accused in drug case.
newsitem.headline: Hearing delayed for Swiss men accused in drug case.

text.p: A court hearing for two Swiss men suspected of sending large quantities of cocaine to Europe hidden in shipments of ornamental plants was delayed for six days on Tuesday, a court official said.

"The inquiry did not happen because the defence lawyer did not show up. The hearing is rescheduled for Monday, Aug. 18," Armando Aguilar, a court official in the Caribbean port city of Puerto Barrios, told Reuters.

Police last week arrested Andreas Haenggi, manager of the Nestle foodstuffs factory in the colonial city of Antigua, Guatemala and his son Nicolas. The two men were in jail in Puerto Barrios, 150 miles (250 kms) east of the capital.
Silvio Geovanelli, also Swiss, and the acting police chief of Antigua, Jose Luis Sebadua, were also arrested in the case and are in jail in Guatemala City awaiting a separate hearing.
Prosecutors said the alleged drug ring used a phantom company, Geovanelli's plant and flower export business, to export drugs to Germany and Spain, prosecutors said.
Police believe the four men were part of a ring that operated for three to five years and exported large quantities of drugs.

German and Guatemalan police are also seeking the alleged leader of the ring, a Spanish man who lived in Antigua and is now a fugitive from justice, Faustino Sanchez, spokesman for the Department of Anti-Narcotic Operations, said.
"I don't have his name because he has different documents with different names, but we believe he was the ring leader," Sanchez said.
According to Sanchez two German intelligence agents have come to Guatemala to help with the investigation, which police hope will lead to further arrests.
